To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a transgenic rat expressing an AVP–eGFP fusion gene in AVPs‐containing MNSs, and that the AVP‐contaning MNCs in this transgenic rat can be identified by virtue of their expression of the AVPeGFP transgene.

the transgenic rats expressing the AVP‐enhance green fluorescent protein fusion gene in arginine vasoppressin‐containing neurosecretory cells exhibit specific and strong fluorescence in the hypothalamic–neurohypophyseial system under physiological and stressful conditions, and thus provide a useful tool for studying AVP‐secereting neurosecretory cells.

we have developed transgenic rats expressing the optically active reporter gene in AVP secreting MNCs, and have shown that the expression of the reporter gene and its protein products in these MNCs can be regulated by osmotic stimuli and stress, and that this system is useful in studies of AVP‐sececting cells in vivo and in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with

elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of AVP synthesis and release in the hypothalamus, and with the elucidation of the role of AVP in the regulation of water and salt homeostasis.
the generation of a transgenic rat expressing an AVP eGFP fusion gene in AVPs‐containing MNSs in the PVN, SON and the median eminence.
the generation and characterisation of transgenic animals that express an optically active reporter gene in AVP and oxytocin‐secreting neurosecretory cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AVP‐enhancer‐driven eGFP reporter gene system can be used as a useful tool to identify AVP‐secereting MNCs and their projections in the hypothalamic neurohypophyseal system.
AVP‐eGP transgenic rats are useful for studying MNCs in the hypothalamus and in the posterior pituiary.

the expression of AVP‐eGFPTg in AVP‐secreatng MNCs is specific and appropriate in the hypothalamic–neurohypophyseial system, and that the transgenic rats are a valuable tool for the study of AVP‐contaning MNCs in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have generated a transgenic animal that expresses the reporter gene specifically and robustly in the MNCs of the hypothal‐amic‐neurohypophysean system, and that the transgenic animals would be a useful tool for the study of AVP‐contaning MNCs.
the AVP‐enhance green fluorescent protein transgenic rats are a powerful tool to study the physiology of AVP‐contaning MNCs in vivo and in vitro.
we succeeded in generating transgenic rats with specific expression of the AVPs‐eGFP gene in AVP containing MNCs in the hypothalamus and in their axon terminals in the posterior pituaitary.
The main takeaway from our work is that

transgenic animals are a useful tool to identify and characterise specific cell populations in the brain, in this case AVP‐secreteing MNCs, which are involved in the control of fluid homeostasis and the activation of the stress system.

transgene expression is specific to the AVP‐contaning MNCs in the hypothalamus and the posterior pituital, and that expression of the transgene is regulated by physiological and pathological stimuli in an appropriate manner, indicating that this transgenic animal is a powerful tool for the analysis of AVP secretion and its regulation.
